subject: Geography
description: Covers Shiwaliks, Zoji La, and Mount Everest.

questions.stem: The Himalayas are divided into three parallel ranges from north to south. Which of the following is the outermost, youngest, and lowest range?

options.option_text: The Shiwaliks
The Himadri (Greater Himalayas)
The Himachal (Lesser Himalayas)
The Karakoram

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Himalayas consist of three main parallel ranges. From north to south, they are: the Himadri (Greater/Inner Himalayas, the highest peaks), the Himachal (Lesser/Middle Himalayas, where hill stations are located), and the Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas). The Shiwaliks are the youngest and lowest mountains, composed largely of unconsolidated river sediments.
DECOY BUSTING: The Himadri contains Mount Everest and Kanchenjunga. The Himachal contains Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar. The Karakoram range (home to K2) is part of the Trans-Himalayas, lying completely north of the Greater Himalayas.
EXAM INSIGHT: The longitudinal valleys lying between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks are known as 'Duns'. Dehradun, Kotli Dun, and Patli Dun are famous examples.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which crucial mountain pass connects Srinagar (Kashmir Valley) to Leh (Ladakh)?

options.option_text: Zoji La
Nathu La
Rohtang Pass
Shipki La

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Zoji La is a high mountain pass in the Himalayas in Ladakh. It provides a vital road link connecting the Kashmir Valley to its west with the Suru and Drass valleys and Leh further east. It remains closed during winter due to heavy snowfall.
DECOY BUSTING: Nathu La (Sikkim) connects India to Tibet/China. Rohtang Pass (Himachal Pradesh) connects the Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti Valleys. Shipki La (Himachal Pradesh) is where the Sutlej river enters India from Tibet.
EXAM INSIGHT: To provide all-weather connectivity and bypass the treacherous Zoji La pass during winter, the Indian government is currently constructing the massive 14 km long Z-Morh and Zoji La tunnels.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world, is located in the Himadri range. In which country/countries does it lie?

options.option_text: On the border of Nepal and China (Tibet)
Entirely within Nepal
On the border of India and Nepal
Entirely within India (Sikkim)

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Mount Everest (8,848.86 m) lies squarely on the international border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. The summit can be accessed from both the southern (Nepalese) side and the northern (Tibetan) side.
DECOY BUSTING: Kanchenjunga, the third highest peak in the world, lies on the border of India (Sikkim) and Nepal. K2 (Mount Godwin-Austen), the second highest, is in the Karakoram range in PoK.
EXAM INSIGHT: In Nepal, Mount Everest is known as 'Sagarmatha' (Goddess of the Sky), and in Tibet, it is known as 'Chomolungma' (Mother Goddess of the World).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Shivalik Hills, the southernmost fold belt of the Himalayan system, are also commonly referred to by which alternative name?

options.option_text: Trans-Himalayas, the zone lying north of the main Himadri
Sub-Himalayas or Outer Himalayas, the youngest Himalayan fold
Tethys Himalayas, the sedimentary fossiliferous inner northern zone
Himachal, the middle range lying between Himadri and the Shivaliks

questions.explanation: The Shivalik Hills are the outermost (southernmost) fold of the Himalayas, formed largely from erosional debris of older Himalayan ranges. Their correct alternative names are Sub-Himalayas or Outer Himalayas. Option D is wrong — 'Himachal' refers to the Middle/Lesser Himalayas lying between Himadri and the Shivaliks, not the Shivaliks themselves.

questions.stem: The Rohtang Pass, now bypassed by the Atal Tunnel (Rohtang Tunnel), connects which pair of regions across the Pir Panjal range?

options.option_text: Manali in Kullu Valley to Lahaul-Spiti across the Pir Panjal range
Srinagar in Kashmir Valley to Kargil town in the Ladakh region
Dharamsala in Kangra Valley to Chamba via the Dhaula Dhar range
Shimla in Himachal Pradesh to Kinnaur via Hindustan-Tibet road

questions.explanation: Rohtang Pass (3,978 m) lies on the Pir Panjal range and connects Manali (Kullu Valley) to the Lahaul-Spiti region. The Atal Tunnel (opened 2020) runs beneath it. Option B is wrong — Srinagar to Kargil is served by the Zoji La pass on the Great Himalayan range, not Rohtang.

questions.stem: Longitudinal valleys locally called 'Duns' (e.g., Dehradun, Patlidun, Kotlidun) are structurally positioned between which two Himalayan ranges?

options.option_text: Between the Trans-Himalayas and the Greater Himalayas (Himadri)
Within the internal anticlines of the Greater Himalayas (Himadri)
Between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shivalik Hills (Outer Himalayas)
Between the Shivalik Hills and the Indo-Gangetic alluvial plain belt

questions.explanation: Duns are tectonic depressions or synclinal valleys formed in the zone between the Lesser Himalayas and the Shivalik Hills. Dehradun is the most well-known example. Option D is wrong — the Shivalik-plains boundary is defined by the Main Frontal Thrust (MFT), not by the formation of Duns.

questions.stem: The Pir Panjal range, which creates a barrier between the Kashmir Valley and the Chenab basin, belongs to which Himalayan sub-zone?

options.option_text: Greater Himalayas (Himadri), the highest perennially snow-clad range
Lesser Himalayas (Himachal), the middle range between Himadri and Shivaliks
Shivalik Hills, the outermost and youngest tertiary folded range
Trans-Himalayan zone, the range lying north of the main watershed

questions.explanation: The Pir Panjal is a major spur of the Lesser Himalayas (Middle Himalayas), lying between Himadri and the Shivaliks. It separates the Kashmir Valley from the Ravi and Chenab drainage basins. Option A is wrong — Himadri comprises the main crystalline backbone (e.g., K2, Nanga Parbat side ranges), not the Pir Panjal spur.

questions.stem: Which glacier in the Karakoram Range is the longest in India and drains southward into the Nubra River in Ladakh?

options.option_text: Gangotri Glacier, the largest glacier in the Garhwal Himalayas region
Siachen Glacier, the longest glacier in India in the Karakoram range
Zemu Glacier, the largest glacier in the eastern Sikkim Himalayas
Milam Glacier, a major glacier in the Kumaon Himalayas of Uttarakhand

questions.explanation: The Siachen Glacier (~76 km long) is the longest glacier in India and the world's second-longest outside polar regions. Located in the Karakoram, its meltwater feeds the Nubra River. Option A is wrong — Gangotri (~30 km) is the longest in the Garhwal Himalayas but is far shorter than Siachen.

questions.stem: In the Himalayan foothills, streams emerging from mountains disappear underground in the porous gravelly 'Bhabar' zone. Where do these streams characteristically re-emerge?

options.option_text: In the Terai belt, surfacing as springs to feed marshy forested swamps
In the Khadar lowlands, directly replenishing the newer floodplain alluvium
In the Bhangar uplands, feeding the older alluvial terrace formations
In the Rann of Kutch, after traveling through long underground aquifers

questions.explanation: Streams lose velocity in the coarse gravel-boulder Bhabar zone and sink underground. They re-emerge as springs at the Bhabar-Terai junction because the finer alluvium of the Terai prevents further percolation, making the Terai a waterlogged, densely forested belt. Option B is wrong — Khadar is active floodplain of major rivers lying far south of the foothills, unrelated to Bhabar seepage.

questions.stem: The Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra are classified as 'antecedent' rivers in the context of the Himalayas. Which explanation BEST justifies this classification?

options.option_text: They originate in glaciers and transport enormous sediment loads to the sea
They predate the Himalayas and kept incising their courses as the ranges rose
They carved deep gorges through earlier glacial U-shaped valley erosion action
They originated on the southern slopes and later cut through the outer Shivaliks

questions.explanation: Antecedent drainage means a river existed before the mountain range formed. As the Himalayas rose gradually during the Cenozoic era, these rivers maintained their original courses by actively downcutting, producing spectacular gorges (e.g., Indus gorge near Nanga Parbat). Option C is wrong — those gorges are V-shaped, products of vertical river erosion, not the wide U-shapes of glacial carving.
